ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.



THE ROLE

We're looking for inference performance engineers who want to make the world's most demanding AI workloads run faster and more efficiently. You'll work across the stack, from the inference engine and runtime through scheduling, serving, and routing. Along the way you'll apply techniques like prefill/decode disaggregation, speculative decoding, and KV-cache management. You'll reason from first principles about where time and memory go, find what's holding performance back, and close the gap. Your work directly impacts how fast our customers' models run and how efficiently we serve them. This role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced startup environment and is eager to make significant contributions to the exciting field of LLM inference.

 

EXAMPLE INITIATIVES

You'll get to work on these types of projects as an Inference Performance engineer:

 - Agentic Kernels in Production https://www.baseten.co/blog/agentic-kernels-in-production/

 - How we built the new fastest API for GLM-5.2 https://www.baseten.co/blog/how-we-built-the-new-fastest-api-for-glm-52/

 - Live draft model training for speculative decoding https://www.baseten.co/blog/live-draft-model-training-for-speculative-decoding/#eliminating-traditional-bottlenecks

 - Making Kimi K3 Tokenization 18x faster https://www.baseten.co/blog/making-kimi-k3-tokenization-18x-faster-for-million-token-agentic-workloads/

 - The Baseten Inference Stack https://www.baseten.co/resources/guide/the-baseten-inference-stack/

 - Driving model performance optimization https://www.baseten.co/blog/driving-model-performance-optimization-2024-highlights/


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Implement and productionize cutting-edge inference techniques, working deep in runtime internals. That includes quantization, speculative decoding, KV-cache reuse, chunked prefill, LoRA, guided generation for structured outputs, and custom scheduling and routing algorithms.

 - Profile and optimize inference end to end, from kernel launch overhead and memory layout up to request scheduling, prefill/decode disaggregation, and cache-aware routing. Run cross-layer investigations, such as tracing a tail-latency regression from request timing through routing and batching down to a kernel.

 - Turn performance into cost savings. Improve tokens per GPU-hour, raise utilization, and give customers and internal teams clear latency/throughput/cost tradeoffs.

 - Bring up and tune new model architectures on new hardware quickly, often in the same week they're released.

 - Build benchmarking frameworks that measure real-world performance across model architectures, batch sizes, sequence lengths, and hardware configurations.

 - Contribute upstream to open-source inference engines (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM), and partner closely with model, infrastructure, and customer-facing teams to ship wins.

 

REQUIREMENTS

 - Bachelor's, Master's, or Ph.D. degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or related field.

 - Experience with one or more general-purpose programming languages, such as Python or C++.

 - Familiarity with LLM optimization techniques (e.g., quantization, speculative decoding, continuous batching).

 - Strong familiarity with ML libraries, especially PyTorch, TensorRT, or TensorRT-LLM.

 - Demonstrated interest and experience in LLMs.

 - Deep understanding of GPU architecture.

 

NICE TO HAVE

 - Proficiency in enhancing the performance of software systems, particularly in the context of large language models (LLMs)

 - Contributed to vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or another inference engine.

 - Worked on large-scale distributed serving: autoscaling, load balancing, multi-region or multi-cloud capacity.

 - Written or optimized GPU kernels (CUDA, Triton, CUTLASS, or similar)

 - Worked on quantization (FP8/FP4, AWQ, GPTQ) or speculative decoding in production.

 - Deep understanding of software engineering principles and a proven track record of developing and deploying AI/ML inference solutions.



BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - (U.S. only) 100% coverage of medical, dental, and vision insurance for employee and dependents

 - Flexible PTO policy including company wide Winter Break (our offices are closed from Christmas Eve to New Year's Day!)

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

 - Exposure to a variety of ML startups, offering unparalleled learning and networking opportunities.

English
Role:
The Systems Engineer will be responsible for the integrated design, coordination, and technical support of both electrical and mechanical auxiliary systems associated with hydro-generator and turbine rehabilitation projects.  Job Description 
 Francais 
 Description du poste 
 Responsabilités principales

 About us 
 We make municipal software built for clerks: websites residents can use, forms and payments that replace stacks of paper, and meeting minutes drafted after every meeting. More than 1,300 local governments rely on us, from counties and cities to villages and towns. We have local government clients in almost every state in the U.S.
 Our clients are municipal clerks and the government teams around them. They keep city hall running and rarely get thanked for it. Your job is to make working with us the easy part of their week.
 The role 
 This is the senior seat on our Client Success team. We are hiring you to raise the standard of our support: fix what is broken, write down how it should work, and show what great looks like.
 Our AI agent now answers repeatable, well-documented questions. What is left is the work that only a person can do: own a client's problem from the first message to the confirmed fix, build a relationship a clerk trusts, and turn what you learn into better documentation and a better product.
 This is not a ticket-closing job. Think of a great 5-star hotel that puts slippers by the bed before you ask. We want a clerk to finish a conversation with you and tell the clerk in the next town about the great experience they had. If that takes three calls, take three calls.
 It is also a technical job. You will work with our developers every day. When something breaks, you work out where it lives before anyone else has to. Is the problem on the events calendar on the client's homepage, or in the calendar widget embedded on a department page? Is the wrong speaker name only in the transcript, or is it also in the finished minutes? You reproduce it, write it up so a developer can act without a follow-up question, stay on it until it ships, and tell the client yourself.
 You need both halves. A brilliant troubleshooter who is short with a clerk will not work here. Neither will a lovely person who forwards every problem to a developer.
 Your first 90 days 
 Learn all of our products well enough to teach them
 Take over every open escalation and close or schedule each one
 Rebuild the path from support to our developers so nothing leaves the queue untracked
 Find the ten questions clerks ask most and fix each at the source: an article, a Fin answer, or a product change
 What you will do 
 Raise the standard 
 Design how issues move from support to developers, and keep that path working
 Set the bar for replies, calls, and write-ups, and coach teammates by example
 Turn what you fix into playbooks the team and Fin can follow
 Delight clients 
 Make every interaction feel personal, warm, and unhurried, especially for less technical users who would rather talk to a person than read a help article
 Step in when the AI agent or the documentation is not enough, and make sure the client feels heard and helped, not processed
 Treat client sentiment as the real measure of success, not ticket speed
 Look for small moments to go above and beyond, and share what works so it becomes how the whole team operates
 Own the problem from start to finish 
 Be the named person on an account when things go wrong: one owner, one plan, regular updates, until the client says it is fixed
 Step in early when an account shows strain (repeat tickets, a rough launch, a frustrated message) and run the recovery. Get on a call, write down what is open, set dates, follow through
 Make sure nothing sits untracked once it leaves the support queue
 Diagnose, then escalate 
 Work out which product and which layer an issue lives in before you hand it to a developer
 Reproduce it, capture the steps with screenshots or a recording, and file it in Linear with everything a developer needs
 Check on your open Linear issues, chase what is stuck, and confirm the fix with the client
 Use Claude, connected to our code repository, to trace where a behavior comes from. For small, well-understood fixes, draft the change for a developer to review
 Knowledge base and AI support 
 Inherit and maintain the help center for all of our products. It is what our AI agent (Fin, in Intercom) answers from
 Write and improve articles from real, recurring questions, on a weekly rhythm measured against live ticket volume

 Independent energy is here. Help us deploy it. 
 Energy should be free. Free from aging grids, fragile supply chains, and unnecessary extraction. At Moment Energy, we’re building a world where clean power is abundant, affordable, and uninterrupted for everyone. 
 The world doesn’t need another promise about energy; it needs proof that a freer future is possible. Moment Energy is the pragmatic liberator of power, the only company certified to turn the largest untapped energy supply into independent energy. 
 Now is the moment. While the industry scraps millions of batteries with decades of life left, we put them to work by repurposing large-format batteries into advanced battery energy storage systems that deliver real-world impact.

 Our Values 
 Our values are key to how we show up every day at Moment Energy! We keep them in the forefront of what we do, and they’re used everywhere.  Safety is our Foundation 
 We prioritize the safety of our products, customers, employees, and the general public above all else. From the workshop to the field, we maintain the highest standards for our batteries in testing manufacturing and deployment, and daily operations.  We place our customers at the core of everything we do, ensuring that every decision considers their needs and aims to provide increased value to them. We provide reliable support for our customers, every step of the way.

 We’re self-starters that proactively embrace new challenges along with personal and collective ownership of responsibilities in the organization. We focus on growth, not titles, and we do what needs to be done.

The Opportunity 
 
Position Summary:
Reporting directly to the Director of Care, the Registered Nurse (RN) is a regulated member of the interprofessional health care team who is responsible for completing comprehensive client assessments, developing and implementing client plans of care that address physical, psychological, emotional, social, behavioural, and recovery-oriented needs.
 
This position monitors ongoing client care and condition to ensure optimum functioning and assumes professional accountability for clients with complex and persistent mental health concerns, co-occurring conditions, and significant psychosocial challenges. The RN administers prescribed medications, supervises the delivery of medications by unregulated staff, collaborates with the interdisciplinary team, and supports clients in achieving their highest level of independence, recovery, wellness, and quality of life.
 
This role requires a strong foundation in trauma-informed, recovery-oriented, culturally safe, and person-directed care, alongside a solid foundation in mental health. The RN must be skilled in therapeutic communication, mental status assessment, behavioural support, crisis intervention, risk assessment, and supporting clients whose needs may fluctuate in complexity and acuity. 
 
In keeping with the Canadian Nurses Association Code of Ethics, CRNA Nursing Practice Standards and Guidelines, Carewest’s Frame of Reference, Philosophy of Care, and Carewest policies, this position maintains professional and ethical standards at all times. Demonstration of leadership is critical for success in this position.
 
Program Summary:
Bridgeland Riverside Continuing Care Centre's Complex Mental Health Programs provide specialized continuing care and interdisciplinary support for adults living with complex mental health conditions, addictions, cognitive impairments, acquired brain injuries, behavioural challenges, and other complex care needs. Services are delivered across a combination of secure and non-secure care environments, based on resident needs, with an emphasis on person-centred, trauma-informed, and harm-reduction approaches. Programs focus on promoting stability, safety, independence, rehabilitation, meaningful engagement, and quality of life while supporting residents in achieving their individual care goals.

• Certification as a Health Care Aide or equivalent is required.
• Ability to read, write and communicate effectively in English is required.

• Knowledge of mental health conditions, addictions, concurrent disorders, and responsive behaviours is an asset.
• Education or training in Mental Health First Aid, trauma-informed care, non-violent crisis intervention, de-escalation techniques, harm reduction, or behavioural support strategies is considered an asset.
• Demonstrated ability to support individuals with complex psychosocial, behavioural, and mental health needs.
• Demonstrated ability to establish therapeutic and professional relationships with clients experiencing mental health challenges.
• Related experience in a health care facility is an asset.
• Experience supporting individuals living with mental illness, addictions, concurrent disorders, behavioural challenges, cognitive impairment,
homelessness, or other complex psychosocial needs is an asset.
• Program specific training and experience is an asset.
• Experience working within a mental health, supportive living, continuing care, or community-based setting is preferred.
• Knowledge of trauma-informed and harm reduction practices is an asset.

The role contributes to the evaluation and management of residential, commercial, institutional, and condominium assets through technical assessments, lifecycle planning, and stakeholder engagement.

Work is performed in accordance with Ontario Regulation 48/01 and involves coordination with property managers, condominium boards, asset owners, and project stakeholders.

 Key Responsibilities 
 Lead reserve fund studies in compliance with Ontario Regulation 48/01 and applicable industry standards.
 Perform building condition assessments and technical field investigations across multiple building systems.
 Conduct site inspections of building envelope systems, structural components, roofing assemblies, interior finishes, and site infrastructure.
 Complete technical evaluations of mechanical and electrical systems to support lifecycle planning and capital investment decisions.
 Assess asset condition, determine remaining service life, and develop asset renewal strategies using lifecycle costing methodologies.
 Prepare capital cost estimates, reserve fund analyses, and long-term cash flow projections.
 Develop and review capital expenditure forecasts and funding scenarios supporting long-range asset planning.
 Produce detailed technical reports outlining findings, risk considerations, and recommended corrective actions.
 Deliver client presentations and communicate funding strategies to condominium boards, property managers, and asset owners.
 Manage project scope, schedule, budget, and stakeholder coordination activities throughout project delivery.
 Monitor project risks and implement mitigation measures during assessment and planning engagements.
 Support proposal development, including scope definition, fee estimation, and technical input.
 Contribute to process improvement initiatives and the implementation of data analytics and AI-enabled assessment methodologies.
Required 
 Degree or diploma in Engineering, Building Science, Quantity Surveying, Construction Management, Architecture, or a related discipline.
 3–5 years of experience in reserve fund studies, capital planning, building condition assessments, or related consulting services.
 Working knowledge of Ontario Regulation 48/01 and associated industry standards governing reserve fund studies.
 Experience conducting field assessments of building envelope, structural, mechanical, and electrical systems.
 Demonstrated ability to prepare cash flow projections, capital expenditure forecasts, and lifecycle cost analyses.
 Strong understanding of lifecycle costing methodologies and asset condition evaluation.
 Proven technical report writing and client presentation experience.
 Valid Ontario driver's license and willingness to travel throughout Ontario.
 Assets 
 Professional designation or active progression toward a designation such as P.Eng., CET, PQS, or RICS.
 Experience working with condominium corporations and boards of directors.
 Exposure to multi-asset portfolios within residential, commercial, and institutional sectors.
 Familiarity with data analytics platforms, digital asset management systems, or AI-enabled assessment tools.
 Experience supporting long-term capital planning programs across diverse property portfolios.

10 places are open for the 2027 term, with a duration of 6 or 12 months at the applicant's option.
 Purpose 
 There is a crisis in academic AI/ML research. What is still worth working on?
 Paper submissions have doubled on the arXiv and at ML conferences, and yet many submitters cannot even answer questions about the details of "their" work.
 Many people across applied research and theory groups, whether math, physics, or computer science, have the distinct feeling that perhaps it is pointless to work on anything other than AI safety and continual learning.
 If we simply draw a line continuing the capabilities progress of the past two years forward, it seems possible that human contributions will be a marginal input in many areas of research within two or three years.
 At the same time, it is clear that fundamental questions in model architecture, sample efficiency, explainability, and creativity are still unanswered, and that making progress on these topics is very likely to benefit humanity over the next two years.
 Designing or training for explainability and determinism may be much easier than achieving post hoc understanding of circuits forced out of scaled data by gradient descent and optimized through blind RL.
 Our focus instead is on frontier research: order-of-magnitude improvements, rather than disposable papers barely better than baseline. 
 The intent of these fellowships is to give awardees uninterrupted time to focus on harder open problems, with adequate compute, talented peers, and weekly 1:1 mentorship from senior researchers but without chasing specific metrics.
 You will be expected to spend about 80% of your time on your own research, and up to 20% of your time either assisting other fellows or participating in wider research programs at IMI.
 We focus largely on applied research and its applications to online security problems, but often publish and support frontier research aligned with our broader interests. Serving hundreds of millions of people gives us a unique perspective as to what works at scale.
 Eligibility:  previous fellows and research staff have come from disparate backgrounds, including early career researchers previously at MSR, FAIR, Mila, MPI, etc. and self taught senior engineers transitioning into research.
 We do not discriminate on the basis of pedigree or age. If you have done interesting work, that is enough.
 Conversely, if you don't already have publications that show you can do good self-directed research then this is not the right opportunity.
 Do not apply if you have no public evidence that you can do good self-directed research and produce results. 
 Location:  you may reside anywhere in the world, excluding sanctioned jurisdictions. This will be a remote fellowship. We do not sponsor visas.
 Deliverables:  we do not have hard targets, and focus on quality. Fellows generally get 1-2 papers with code done in a year, targeting NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, etc. At the end of your fellowship, if the threshold for refereed publication is unmet we will expect a final report, which may be published as a blog post.
 Full details are available at: https://www.imachines.com/imi-ai-ml-fellowships-2025-2026-high-risk-research 
 (imachines dot com slash imi-ai-ml-fellowships-2025-2026-high-risk-research)
 Please note that if you are unable to find this page on our website you will be unable to correctly answer the questions required to submit an application, and your application will be automatically discarded.
 Applying:  send a brief bio / CV link via this page. Include 1) the topic you are interested in working on, 2) a few lines on any relevant prior work you've done, 3) your github / scholar / x links, 4) your desired start date, duration, and other obligations (if any) during that period, and 5) a brief analysis of one of the projects outlined on the page linked above.
 Each project we have listed intentionally includes some gaps or glosses. List the ones you see, and how you'd solve them. Alternatively, if you dislike the projects outlined under a particular topic, briefly write up your own idea and why it is more promising, along with your estimate of time and compute required.
 Deadline:  Admitting fellows in two cohorts. Deadlines for consideration: April 1 and September 1 2026. 3 week decision period. Rolling thereafter.
 Compensation:  competitive location-adjusted stipend, conference and travel support for conferences with accepted papers.
 After the fellowship:  past fellows have stayed on in full-time roles at IMI or co-founded AI unicorns. This is a selective process, so we claim little credit for their success. However, we will support your next steps.
 Selection criteria:  novelty and importance, clarity of approach, feasibility given time/compute, alignment with topics. Panel review and one interview.
 Using AI: Coding agents are useful tools. We provide access to the top models, and were early adopters of evals-first development flows.
 Familiarity with coding using agents is part of all interviews. However, reliability and correctness are critical for us. You will need to read and understand every line of code with your name on it, and it will be reviewed by both people and machines.
 Selection is based on merit. We promote equality of opportunity, and welcome applications from anyone with talent, skills and potential. IMI is an equal opportunity employer, and does not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, sex, orientation, race, religion or belief. 
 Please note that all positions require pre-employment screening, including third-party verification of work history, education, and identity, as well as a final in-person interview and identity verification step, which will be conducted in your country of residence.

The Go To Market (GTM) Performance & Strategy team helps teams turn strategy into consistent execution through targeted coaching, practice, and performance improvement. As a Senior Field Performance Partner, you’ll work with frontline Sales and Channel leaders across US and Canada to diagnose performance gaps, build focused development plans, and use data and AI to help teams improve. Your work will help 1Password’s go-to-market organization perform at its best while advancing our mission to enable a safe, productive digital future.

This is not a traditional enablement role. We don’t believe more training is always the answer. We believe enablement should start with the performance problem, use data and AI to understand what’s happening, and apply the most targeted intervention possible.

You’ll independently own the performance improvement cycle for the teams you support: diagnose → prescribe → activate → reinforce → measure → adjust.

You’ll combine business results, AI-generated coaching insights, field observations, and manager input to identify where teams and individuals need support. You’ll turn those insights into focused enablement plans, use AI to scale individualized practice and coaching, help managers reinforce the right behaviors, and measure whether performance actually changed.

As 1Password continues to scale our partner-led GTM motion, you’ll also help make channel execution part of how our field operates every day. Rather than treating channel as a separate motion or specialist skill, you’ll help managers and teams build the behaviors needed to effectively identify, engage, and sell with partners as part of their everyday work.

Your job isn’t to keep people busy with enablement. It’s to help them perform better.

Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.

 - 7+ years of experience in a Business-to-Business (B2B) technology go-to-market (GTM) organization across Sales, Customer Success, Solutions Engineering, BDR, Enablement, frontline leadership, or a combination of these areas.

We are looking for a Self-Driving Systems Specialist (SDS Specialist) to support the diagnostics, calibration, configuration, and technical readiness of self-driving systems used in autonomous vehicles and robotaxi fleets across North America.
The SDS Specialist focuses on the technology layer of autonomous mobility: sensors, compute systems, software configurations, autonomous driving hardware, system diagnostics, calibration procedures, and technical validation. This role ensures that the self-driving system installed in each autonomous vehicle is functioning correctly, accurately calibrated, and ready to support safe testing, commercial deployment, and autonomous ride-hailing operations.
You will work closely with Senior Technicians, AV Operations Leads, Safety Operators, Depot Specialists, engineering teams, and fleet operations teams to identify technical issues, execute structured troubleshooting procedures, and support reliable operation of autonomous vehicle platforms.
This position is ideal for candidates with experience in automotive electronics, ADAS systems, embedded systems, robotics, diagnostics, calibration, or complex technical support who want to work at the center of autonomous vehicle deployment and robotaxi operations.

Key Responsibilities: Self-Driving System Diagnostics 
 Diagnose and troubleshoot self-driving system issues affecting autonomous vehicle performance and fleet readiness.
 Investigate technical problems related to cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS/GNSS, compute units, sensors, connectivity modules, wiring, and autonomous driving hardware.
 Execute structured diagnostic procedures to identify root causes of SDS hardware, software, and configuration issues.
 Support advanced troubleshooting for autonomous vehicle faults that impact testing, commercial operations, or robotaxi fleet availability .

 The Labourer will perform work both indoors and outdoors throughout all Regina Exhibition Association Limited (REAL) grounds and facilities. The Labourer is responsible for performing general duties including, but not limited to: moving, setting-up and tearing down of equipment for various events, building event conversions, material maintenance, snow removal and green space maintenance. This position supports the unit in an efficient and safe manner to meet conversions and event schedules. 
 Perform various interior duties which includes, but is not limited to the following:
 Setting up, arranging and removing decorations, tables, chairs, staging and scaffolding to prepare facilities for the various scheduled events.
 Installing and removal of a variety of materials including but not limited to rink boards and glass, event signage, minor scaffolding, and construction materials.
 Various asset repairs and maintenance. 
 Various office equipment moves.
 Inspecting of properties as assigned
 Perform various exterior duties, which includes but is not limited to the following: 
 Removing snow from sidewalks, driveways and parking areas using snow blowers, snow shovels, and ice melt. 
 Clearing debris and shovel snow from streets and sidewalks.
 Setup various outdoor events including barricade/security fencing, field protection cover outdoors and staging. 
 Loading, unloading, setting-up and moving supplies, materials, equipment, or furniture to and from work site.
 Off-site pick up of materials and some off-site event set up.
 Campus greenspace and landscaping maintenance such as grass cutting, tree pruning, fertilizing and watering etc.
 Minor repairs of chain link fencing around the perimeter of the property.
 Maintaining overall cleanliness and appearance of REAL campus 
 Responsible for equipment while on shift by:
 Performing routine preventative maintenance to ensure that all green space and snow removal equipment continue to run smoothly.
 Using tools ranging from common hand and power tools
 Assist equipment operators to ensure attachments to equipment or trucks are properly secured. 
 **Presenting services in a professional, respectful and positive manner at all times when interacting with internal and external customers.
 ** Additional duties and responsibilities as assigned.  
 **This is a Casual position, hours are not guaranteed and will be scheduled according to the needs of the business** 
 Wage: $16.12 -$17.50 
 No. of Vacancies: 10 
 WHAT IT TAKES  
  Apply today if you meet the following requirements: 
 Completion of Grade 12 or equivalent. 
 Must possess and maintain a valid Class 5 Saskatchewan Provincial driver’s license. 
 Experience in the operations of arena, commercial or industrial building maintenance.  
 Ability to be safety conscious and willing to follow safety policies and procedures. 
 Ability to perform the physically strenuous and demanding tasks to fulfill all working conditions and physical demands. 
 Demonstrated ability to take direction, follow instructions and work independently or with a team. 
 Willingness and ability to maintain a respectable public image and conduct, interacting with customers in a courteous and friendly manner. 
 Possession of a valid CPR & First Aid certification card is an asset. 
 Must be able to obtain and maintain a satisfactory Criminal Record Check for the duration of employment.  
 Note that this position is an in-scope position under the RWDSU Collective Agreement.  
 WHY CHOOSE REAL?   
 Here at REAL, we can offer unique experiences unlike any other organization:  
 Make a difference in your own community. 
 Be a part of an industry responsible to create fun and memorable moments for our guests. 
 A wide range of employment opportunities to fit your own lifestyle – whether that’s committing to us in a full-time capacity or more of a casual role that is event specific and tailored around your own availability.     
 We offer competitive wages and industry standard benefits.  
 Matching Group RRSP plan. 
 For more information visit our website at www.realdistrict.ca . Submit resumes by November 1, 2026 via the link provided. 
 Please click the link to apply: https://apply.workable.com/real1884/j/3B1D4EB7C5 
 While REAL appreciates the interest by all applicants, only those selected to advance to the next stage will be contacted. Note preference will be given to internal applicants holding existing REAL RWDSU seniority.
